svg.text: TEACHER ANCHOR: CCSS.HSA.SSE.A.2 • TEKS 111.39.c.10.E • UNSPSC 60101700 • TITLE I / IV GRANT ELIGIBLE • MODEL: SC32
LESSON GUIDE: FACTORING TRINOMIALS & BINOMIAL ARRAYS
Grades 7–11 Pre-Algebra & Algebra II • Hands-On Classroom & Home STEM Studio Series

text.tspan: Slide the two L-rails into the lid corner to form the origin.
Place the emerald +x² tile flush into the corner.
Its 35.00 × 35.00 mm area establishes the quadratic core.
We need to distribute 5 positive x rods around the +x² tile.
Place 3 rods along the top rail (horizontal dimension).
Place 2 rods along the left rail (vertical dimension).
3. COMPLETE THE RECTANGLE: Fill missing corner with 6 constant (+1) tiles!
4. READ BINOMIAL DIMENSIONS: Horizontal width is (x + 3); vertical length is (x + 2).
Calculator Verification: Press Polynomial Solver Icon ([↱][EQN] & [↱][POLY]) and run [↱] [POLY] 1 [A] 5 [B] 6 [C] 0 [D] [EXEC] [RCL] 1 [RCL] 3 → -2.

g.text: THE BIG AHA! FACTORING IS UN-MULTIPLYING AREA

text.tspan: Factoring a quadratic is literally finding the length and width of a rectangle! If the tiles
cannot form a solid rectangle without gaps, the trinomial is prime. Zero-pairs (+x and -x)
let you model differences of squares x² - 4 with effortless physical cancellation!

g.text: ★ NOW YOU TRY! (STUDENT PRACTICE CHALLENGE): FACTOR: x² + 6x + 8

text.tspan: Arrange one +x² tile, six +x rods, and eight +1 units into a solid rectangle. What are its rail dimensions? (Scan QR for 3D animated solution!)

g.text: → Build with your blocks, then scan the QR code to watch the animated 3D solution on your screen!
